reason: TRβ2 (thyroid hormone receptor beta-2) is a primary transcriptional regulator of LWS cone opsin expression; the paper directly studies ligand-dependent control of lws1/lws2 (zebrafish OPN1LW orthologs) and cone subtype fate specification. The mechanistic link to OPN1LW is direct and well-established.

Paper is about the Elongator complex regulating larval-pupal metamorphosis via ecdysteroid biosynthesis in Tribolium castaneum (red flour beetle). Although ELP4 is a subunit of the Elongator complex, the biological context is entirely insect developmental biology with no ophthalmic or human disease relevance.

Color vision deficiency (CVD) as measured by the Ishihara test is the primary phenotype caused by OPN1LW mutations. A large-cohort prevalence study of Ishihara test failures directly characterises the epidemiology of OPN1LW-related disease and is within scope for the gene collection.

Paper directly studies L-cone (long-wavelength-sensitive cone) function and spatial distribution using adaptive optics; L cones express OPN1LW. Findings on local L/M ratio effects on color detection and naming are directly relevant to OPN1LW biology and color vision physiology.

Tutorial explicitly addresses genetically determined spectral shifts of L-cone photopigment (encoded by OPN1LW), individual differences in cone spectral sensitivities arising from OPN1LW variants, and their impact on color vision. Directly relevant to OPN1LW function and clinical consequences.

Classic Drosophila paper on Dachshund and Eyes Absent forming a complex to drive ectopic eye development; Sine oculis (So), the Drosophila SIX6 homolog, operates in the same retinal determination network. The paper is foundational for understanding PAX6 and SIX6 network function in eye specification, both of which are listed gene targets.

Review of small heat shock proteins (sHsps) covers structural principles and their role in eye lens transparency. CRYAB (alphaB-crystallin, HSPB5) is a prototypical sHsp and a major lens protein; the review directly discusses lens function and protein homeostasis relevant to both CRYAB and CRYBB3.

Comparative genomics study identifying candidate genes for retinal degeneration loci using photoreceptor dystrophy mouse models (rd1, rd2). PDE6A encodes the rod PDE6 alpha subunit, and the closely related rd1 model involves rod PDE signalling. The paper is directly about retinal degeneration gene discovery and validates PDE6-pathway relevance.

Paper measures absolute abundance of crystallins in human and transgenic mouse lenses; CRYBB3 is a lens beta-crystallin that would be among the proteins quantified. The alphaA N101D transgenic mouse is a cataract model, and crystallin stoichiometry data directly informs understanding of lens crystallin biology including CRYBB3.

Paper characterises TBC1D20 as a Rab1 GAP that regulates vesicle trafficking; this biochemical function is directly responsible for the ER-to-Golgi trafficking defect that causes Warburg Micro syndrome (microphthalmia). Understanding TBC1D20 Rab-GAP activity is mechanistically essential for the gene's ophthalmic disease link.

Comprehensive review of the Hippo pathway where YAP (YAP1) and TAZ are the central transcriptional effectors. YAP1 mutations cause coloboma. The paper covers YAP1 biology in depth including mechanotransduction and organ size control, providing essential mechanistic context for the gene.

Targeted disruption of Yap65 (the gene now known as YAP1) in mice; reveals in vivo requirements for YAP1 in developmental processes. A primary functional characterisation of YAP1 through knockout; directly relevant to understanding how YAP1 mutations cause developmental eye defects.

Direct biochemical characterisation of high-molecular-weight disulfide-linked crystallin aggregates in cataractous human lenses. CRYGD (gamma-D crystallin) is known to aggregate and cause cataract. The study of crystallin crosslinking and aggregation is foundational to understanding CRYGD-related cataract mechanisms.

Review of crystallins in retinal ganglion cell survival and regeneration; CRYBB2 (betaB2-crystallin) has documented roles in RGC neuroprotection and axonal regeneration. Directly relevant to CRYBB2's ophthalmic biology beyond its lens function.

Experimental study showing betaB2-crystallin (CRYBB2) promotes optic nerve axon regeneration after crush injury in rats. Directly studies CRYBB2 protein function in an ophthalmic in vivo model; highly relevant to the gene's role in retinal ganglion cell and optic nerve biology.

Biophysical study of lens beta-crystallin homodimer and heterodimer solution dynamics. CRYBA1 (betaA1/A3-crystallin) forms homodimers and heterodimers with other beta-crystallins; hydrogen-deuterium exchange data directly informs the structural biology of CRYBA1 and its stability in the lens.

Paper studies CRYbetaB2 (CRYBB2) exclusively in the context of triple-negative breast cancer tumorigenesis via nucleolin upregulation. The gene appears but the biological context is cancer biology with no ophthalmic relevance; the library is focused on ophthalmogenetics and this subject matter falls clearly outside scope.

Foundational cloning paper for CNG-3 (CNGA3), a cyclic nucleotide-gated channel alpha subunit causing achromatopsia. The paper characterises CNGA3 electrophysiology and tissue expression; this is primary molecular characterisation of the gene and is directly relevant to the CNGA3 gene collection.

Review of Usher syndrome molecular genetics directly covering all five listed genes: ADGRV1 (USH2C), CDH23 (USH1D), MYO7A (USH1B), USH1C (harmonin), and USH2A. The paper is squarely about the genetics of the ophthalmic/audio-vestibular syndrome these genes cause.

Longitudinal OCT study of progressive cone photoreceptor degeneration in achromatopsia; achromatopsia is the primary phenotype of CNGA3, CNGB3, and PDE6H mutations, all listed as gene targets. The paper directly characterises the natural history of the disease these genes cause and supports gene therapy rationale.
